topics.label: Introduction to the lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the class and introduces complement as a challenging but essential topic for the session.

topics.label: Foundational principles of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts required to understand the complement cascade prior to examining specific pathways.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three upstream recognition mechanisms that converge on C3 activation to trigger the complement cascade.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the primary downstream mechanisms through which activated complement eliminates pathogens.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory mechanisms that prevent complement from inadvertently attacking and destroying host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how deficiencies in specific complement components manifest in distinct clinical presentations.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how pathogens circumvent complement-mediated immunity, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary example.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the complement lecture and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
